framework.name: EU Artificial Intelligence Act
framework.issuing_body: European Parliament and Council of the EU
framework.description: The world's first comprehensive legal framework for AI, establishing a risk-based approach to regulating AI systems placed on the EU market or affecting persons in the EU. Imposes obligations on providers, deployers, importers, and distributors of AI systems, with requirements scaling with risk level.
framework.enforcement_body: National competent authorities + European AI Office
framework.penalty_max: EUR 35,000,000 or 7% of global annual turnover

requirements.title: Prohibited AI Practices
requirements.text: The following AI practices are prohibited: (a) AI systems that deploy subliminal techniques beyond a person's consciousness to materially distort behaviour causing harm; (b) AI systems that exploit vulnerabilities of specific groups; (c) AI systems for social scoring by public authorities; (d) real-time remote biometric identification systems in publicly accessible spaces by law enforcement (except in listed exceptional circumstances); (e) AI systems for emotion recognition in workplaces and educational institutions; (f) biometric categorisation systems inferring sensitive attributes; (g) AI systems creating facial recognition databases by untargeted scraping.
requirements.scope: All AI systems placed on the EU market or used in the EU

controls.description: Maintain an inventory of all AI systems classified against Article 5 prohibitions
evidence_needed: AI use case register with prohibition screening
Legal counsel sign-off on prohibited practices assessment

controls.description: Establish a prohibition screening process in the AI procurement and development lifecycle
Document exceptions claimed under Article 5(2)-(6) for biometric identification

requirements.title: Classification Rules for High-Risk AI Systems
requirements.text: An AI system shall be considered high-risk if it: (a) is a safety component of a product covered by Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I and is subject to third-party conformity assessment; or (b) falls within the categories in Annex III. Providers must register high-risk AI systems in the EU database before placing on market.
requirements.scope: All AI system providers and deployers

controls.description: Conduct and document classification analysis for each AI system against Annex I and Annex III criteria
Register high-risk AI systems in the EU AI database prior to market placement
Monitor for changes to Annex III delegated acts that may reclassify existing systems

requirements.title: Risk Management System
requirements.text: A risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented, and maintained for high-risk AI systems throughout the lifecycle. It shall consist of a continuous iterative process including: identification and analysis of reasonably foreseeable risks; estimation and evaluation of risks; evaluation of risks after testing; adoption of suitable risk management measures. Residual risk must be judged acceptable.

controls.description: Implement a documented risk management process covering identification, analysis, evaluation, and treatment of AI risks
Conduct risk analysis covering the intended purpose and reasonably foreseeable misuse
Test the AI system against defined risk scenarios prior to deployment
Document residual risks and obtain acceptance from senior stakeholders

requirements.title: Data and Data Governance
requirements.text: High-risk AI systems that use training, validation, and testing data sets shall comply with data governance and management practices, including: design choices; data collection processes; examination for biases; identification of relevant data gaps or shortcomings; and appropriate measures to address them. Training, validation, and testing data sets shall be relevant, representative, free of errors, and complete.
requirements.scope: High-risk AI system providers using trained models

controls.description: Document data governance practices covering collection, labelling, preprocessing, and versioning of training/validation/test datasets
Conduct and document bias analysis on training and test datasets with documented remediation
Maintain records of dataset provenance, version, and statistical characteristics
Implement data quality controls to ensure data is relevant, representative, and free of errors

requirements.title: Record-Keeping and Logging
requirements.text: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed with capabilities enabling the automatic recording of events (logs) throughout the system's lifetime. Logging capabilities shall ensure traceability of the AI system's functioning throughout the lifecycle, enable monitoring of the operation of the high-risk AI system, and support post-market monitoring.

controls.description: Implement automated logging of AI system inputs, outputs, and decision events with tamper-evident storage
Define and enforce log retention periods appropriate to the risk level and jurisdiction
Enable reconstruction of any individual AI decision from logs for audit or regulatory review

requirements.title: Transparency and Provision of Information to Deployers
requirements.text: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret the system's output and use it appropriately. A comprehensive instructions for use document shall be provided, including: identity and contact details of provider; characteristics, capabilities, and limitations; accuracy metrics; known risks; human oversight measures required; expected lifetime.

controls.description: Produce and maintain an Instructions for Use document for each high-risk AI system
Disclose system capabilities, limitations, and known failure modes to deployers
For AI chatbots and other limited-risk systems, disclose to users that they are interacting with AI
Provide accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity performance metrics

requirements.title: Human Oversight
requirements.text: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period of use. Providers shall ensure that natural persons assigned to oversight are able to: fully understand the capacities and limitations of the system; monitor its operation; detect and address anomalies, malfunctions, and unexpected performance; interpret outputs; and be able to disregard, override, or reverse the outputs.
requirements.scope: High-risk AI system providers and deployers

controls.description: Define and document human oversight roles, responsibilities, and override procedures for each high-risk AI system
Implement technical mechanisms enabling humans to pause, override, or reject AI outputs
Provide training to all personnel responsible for AI oversight
Monitor and measure effectiveness of human oversight in practice

requirements.title: Accuracy, Robustness, and Cybersecurity
requirements.text: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed to achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, and to perform consistently in these respects throughout their lifecycle. High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against attempts by third parties to alter their use, outputs, or performance through adversarial attacks. Technical solutions shall address the problem of AI-specific vulnerabilities.

controls.description: Define and measure accuracy metrics appropriate to the use case; document acceptance thresholds
Conduct robustness testing including edge cases, distributional shift, and adversarial inputs
Implement cybersecurity controls addressing AI-specific threats (model inversion, data poisoning, evasion attacks)
Establish ongoing monitoring for accuracy and robustness degradation in production

requirements.title: High-Risk AI System Categories
requirements.text: AI systems referred to in Article 6(2). Categories include: (1) biometric identification and categorisation; (2) management of critical infrastructure; (3) education and vocational training; (4) employment, worker management, and access to self-employment; (5) access to and enjoyment of essential private services and essential public services and benefits; (6) law enforcement; (7) migration, asylum, and border control management; (8) administration of justice and democratic processes.
requirements.scope: AI system providers whose systems fall within listed categories

controls.description: Map each AI system in scope against all eight Annex III categories with documented justification
Apply all Chapter III Section 2 requirements to any system classified under Annex III
evidence_needed: Compliance programme evidence for each Article 9–15 requirement

requirements.title: EU Declaration of Conformity and CE Marking
requirements.text: Before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, the provider shall draw up an EU declaration of conformity in accordance with Article 47. The provider shall affix CE marking to the high-risk AI system. The EU declaration of conformity shall be kept by the provider for ten years after the high-risk AI system has been placed on the market or put into service.

controls.description: Complete EU Declaration of Conformity process before market placement of high-risk AI systems
Maintain DoC and supporting technical documentation for minimum 10 years post-market
Register the AI system in the EU AI public database prior to placing on market
